entities.name: Dutch Golden Age Maritime Trade
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: The Netherlands became the world's foremost maritime trading power in the 17th century through the Dutch East India Company (VOC) and Dutch West India Company. Dutch traders dominated the spice trade, established colonies, and pioneered financial instruments like stock exchanges.

entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: The Netherlands' extraordinary rise (c. 1580–1700) from small republic to the world's dominant trading power. The Dutch East India Company (VOC, 1602) became the first publicly traded company; Amsterdam's bourse became the first stock exchange; and Dutch ships carried more cargo than all other European nations combined. This era created modern capitalism's infrastructure: stock markets, joint-stock companies, central banking, and insurance.
